findings.claim: A wheel that starts over a `.loft` provider iframe (YouTube) is never seen by the layer's wheel forwarder. The iframe sits in the `position: fixed` layer outside the canvas scroller, so the browser chains that scroll to the document instead of the slot's scrolling ancestor.
findings.impact: On a desktop file page with a YouTube `.loft`, a wheel over the embed probably does not scroll the canvas the way it did before the layer, while the same wheel over a native video does. I7 requires the same scroll for both.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/player/layer/PlayerLayer.tsx:261 registers the wheel listener on the layer frame in the parent document. Wheel events inside a cross-origin iframe are dispatched in the iframe's own document and never bubble to that listener. frontend/src/app/globals.css:1416-1419 makes `[data-player-layer]` `position: fixed`, so the iframe's scroll chain no longer passes through the canvas scroller. The only I7 e2e case (frontend/e2e-components/player-layer-desktop.spec.ts:443-488) opens the default file page and does not exercise a provider iframe.

bucket_proposal.reason: I7 requires a wheel that starts on the player to scroll the slot's nearest scrolling ancestor by the same amount as without the layer, and the player includes the `.loft` provider iframe (I1).

findings.proposed_fix: Verify in a real browser with a YouTube `.loft` and add an I7 e2e case over the iframe. If the canvas does not scroll, forward the scroll some other way, for example with a transparent wheel-catching overlay while the iframe is not being interacted with, or by scrolling the canvas when the document scrolls.

verification.note: frontend/src/components/player/layer/PlayerLayer.tsx:247 returns (leaving the event alone) only when |deltaX| > |deltaY|. Otherwise, past the ctrl, full-screen and inner-scroller checks, line 252 calls preventDefault and line 259 applies only `deltaY * unit` to `scroller.scrollTop`. Nothing applies deltaX, so the horizontal part of a diagonal wheel is lost. It matters only where the slot's scroller (or an ancestor) also scrolls horizontally.

unspecified_scores.reason: A wheel over the player in pseudo or system full screen is not forwarded (PlayerLayer.tsx:249); the covered page cannot be seen anyway and the e2e case confirms the page stays put, so the user sees nothing wrong.

Hand-made scroll chaining: wheeling over the player's settings panel scrolls it to its end and then the canvas jumps instantly by the raw delta, ignoring overscroll-behavior and smooth scrolling; it feels slightly different from a native scroll.
A diagonal trackpad swipe over the player moves only vertically, which shows only if the canvas also overflows horizontally, and that is rare on the file page.

specification_compliance: I7 holds for a native `<video>` (the vertical wheel is forwarded with deltaMode scaling; ctrl, sideways, full-screen and inner-scroller cases are excluded). For a provider iframe it is in doubt (V-1).

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A wheel whose horizontal and vertical parts are equal and non-zero is treated as vertical and preventDefaulted, so the horizontal part is dropped as well.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: An exactly diagonal trackpad input over the player scrolls only vertically, which is barely noticeable.

regression_risks: A scroll over a YouTube `.loft` embed may not reach the canvas because the iframe now lives in a fixed layer outside the scroller.
test_coverage: player-layer-desktop.spec.ts:443 covers the vertical wheel over the default player only; no case covers a diagonal wheel or a wheel over a provider iframe.
player-layer-wheel.spec.ts covers the settings-panel chaining and pseudo full screen; player-layer-wheel-desktop.spec.ts covers ctrl+wheel.
not_verified: Did not run any browser to confirm V-1's scroll chaining for a cross-origin iframe inside a fixed layer.
Did not check whether the default fixture in the I7 desktop test is a native video or a `.loft` embed.
Did not verify behavior in Safari/WebKit.
